plan.title: Genotype x drug interaction DE and pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is precisely an interaction question in a 2x2 factorial design (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, 4 replicates/cell, 16 samples, 12000 genes, human brain, salmon-derived raw counts). The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 interaction workflow: (1) QC on variance-stabilized data to confirm the four groups separate and no sample is an outlier before any test is trusted; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering (independent filtering handles the rest); (3) a DESeq2 negative-binomial model with design ~genotype+treatment+genotype:treatment fitted directly on raw counts (median-of-ratios normalization is internal to the model, never pre-applied); (4) the interaction coefficient tested first with the Wald test — this coefficient IS the answer to 'does the drug act differently in KO vs WT', since it is the difference-in-differences of the drug effect between genotypes — followed by the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle in WT; drug vs vehicle in KO) so the interaction has an interpretable anchor; (5) LFC shrinkage (apeglm for the single interaction coefficient, ashr for the composite simple-effect contrasts); (6) BH-FDR per contrast with independent filtering; (7) fgsea preranked enrichment on the Wald statistic per contrast against MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome (both staged locally for human); (8) a final integrated report naming the reference levels, all three contrasts side-by-side, fit diagnostics, and the reproducibility record. Given only 4 replicates per cell, the interaction test is explicitly flagged as underpowered (large SE on a difference-of-differences), consistent with the grounded rule R-0013.
